ai.description: Deven's Night Frog is a small amphibian (20–25 mm) with a brownish-grey dorsum and pale ventral surface. It features prominent, rounded toe pads and a distinct, pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus deveni* is best distinguished by its distinctively pointed, snout-like projection at the tip of the head, which is more pronounced than in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Nyctibatrachus deveni* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found along rocky streams at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Deven's Night Frogs are nocturnal, spending their nights foraging for small insects along the rocky, fast-flowing streams of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus deveni* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 15–30 eggs on wet rocks or vegetation, which undergo direct development without a free-swimming stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: Nyctibatrachus deveni is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, where it inhabits high-elevation evergreen forests above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Deven’s Night Frog produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short "tink" notes, typically heard calling from mossy rocks near fast-flowing streams.
